items.title: Two irreducible algebraic spaces are birational exactly when they share an isomorphic nonempty open subspace
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for algebraic spaces X and Y over S with irreducible underlying topological spaces, X and Y are birational if and only if they contain nonempty open subspaces U and V isomorphic over S (source lines 9888-9895). One direction is the definition; the other is a reduction that shrinks the two opens step by step: from inverse dominant rational maps f : U -> Y and g : V -> X one arranges that f factors through V and that U -> V -> X is the inclusion, then symmetrically produces V' contained in V over which g factors through U with V' -> U -> Y the identity, and finally takes U' to be the open subspace of U whose underlying set is the preimage of |V'|, so that the two morphisms become mutually inverse.
